title: Cryptography and Randomness Misuse
platform_conditions: .NET Framework 4.x and modern .NET; CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals requires .NET Core 2.1+
security_mechanism: System.Random is a time-seeded subtractive generator whose outputs reveal enough internal state to predict future draws, so tokens, reset codes, or keys taken from rnd.Next() are guessable from a handful of observed values. CipherMode defaults and hand-rolled parameters reintroduce classical breaks: ECB leaks equality of plaintext blocks, a fixed IV with CBC makes the first block deterministic for identical inputs, and certificate-validation callbacks that return true (RemoteCertificateValidationCallback / ServerCertificateValidationCallback) switch TLS into accept-anything mode. Comparing MACs or digests with == compares byte arrays via looped equality, leaking a timing oracle that recovers authenticator bytes.

source_sink_clues.source: The security value itself: session tokens, password reset codes, API keys, MAC tags, and the crypto parameters (mode, IV, callbacks) chosen in code.
source_sink_clues.sink: new Random() feeding security values; Aes/DESCryptoServiceProvider configured with CipherMode.ECB or a constant IV; certificate-validation callbacks that return true; == / SequenceEqual on digests or MACs

tracking_guards: Require RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes for any security value; require CipherMode.CBC/GCM with a random per-message IV from RNGCryptoServiceProvider (or AesGcm); require validation callbacks to inspect the certificate and ssl policy errors rather than returning true unconditionally; require CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals for authenticator comparison.
not_candidate_when: Random is confined to non-security uses (sampling, jitter, simulations), ECB/fixed-IV applies only to non-secret, non-repeating data with no confidentiality requirement, the callback's unconditional-true branch is gated to a documented test environment, or comparison already uses FixedTimeEquals.
synthetic_vulnerable_example: Random rnd = new Random(); string token = rnd.Next().ToString();
public_references: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/338.html
CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/327.html
